passages.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied: “If one ventures a word with you, will you be wearied? Yet who can keep from speaking?
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz was a man from Teman.
Eliphaz replied to Job.
Eliphaz said, “If someone speaks to you, will you become tired?
Who can keep from speaking?”
passages.original: וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ הֲנִסָּ֬ה דָבָ֣ר אֵלֶ֣יךָ תִּלְאֶ֑ה וַעְצֹ֥ר בְּ֝מִלִּ֗ין מִ֣י יוּכָֽל׃

passages.text: Surely you have instructed many, and have strengthened their feeble hands.
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz the Temanite spoke to Job.
Eliphaz said that Job had taught many people.
Job had given instruction to others.
Job had helped people who were weak.
Job had strengthened hands that were feeble.
passages.original: הִ֭נֵּה יִסַּ֣רְתָּ רַבִּ֑ים וְיָדַ֖יִם רָפ֣וֹת תְּחַזֵּֽק׃

passages.text: Your words have steadied those who stumbled; you have braced the knees that were buckling.
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz the Temanite spoke to Job.
Eliphaz said that Job’s words helped people.
Job’s words lifted up those who stumbled.
Job’s words made weak knees strong.
Job encouraged people who were falling.
Job gave strength to those who were about to collapse.
passages.original: כּ֭וֹשֵׁל יְקִימ֣וּן מִלֶּ֑יךָ וּבִרְכַּ֖יִם כֹּרְע֣וֹת תְּאַמֵּֽץ׃

passages.text: But now trouble has come upon you, and you are weary. It strikes you, and you are dismayed.
passages.sermon:
Trouble has come to you now.
You feel weary.
Trouble touches you.
You become dismayed.
passages.original: כִּ֤י עַתָּ֨ה׀ תָּב֣וֹא אֵלֶ֣יךָ וַתֵּ֑לֶא תִּגַּ֥ע עָ֝דֶ֗יךָ וַתִּבָּהֵֽל׃

passages.text: Is your reverence not your confidence, and the uprightness of your ways your hope?
passages.sermon:
You fear God.
This fear gives you confidence.
You live uprightly.
Your upright ways give you hope.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֣א יִ֭רְאָתְךָ כִּסְלָתֶ֑ךָ תִּ֝קְוָתְךָ֗ וְתֹ֣ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Consider now, I plead: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Or where have the upright been destroyed?
passages.sermon:
I ask you to remember something important.
Think about this question.
Has any innocent person ever perished?
Has anyone upright ever been destroyed?
No innocent person has perished.
No upright person has been destroyed.
passages.original: זְכָר־ נָ֗א מִ֤י ה֣וּא נָקִ֣י אָבָ֑ד וְ֝אֵיפֹ֗ה יְשָׁרִ֥ים נִכְחָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: As I have observed, those who plow iniquity and those who sow trouble reap the same.
passages.sermon:
I have seen people do evil.
I have seen people cause trouble.
These people harvest what they plant.
They receive the results of their actions.
Evil actions bring evil results.
Trouble brings more trouble.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָ֭אִיתִי חֹ֣רְשֵׁי אָ֑וֶן וְזֹרְעֵ֖י עָמָ֣ל יִקְצְרֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of His anger they are consumed.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful and just.
God judges the wicked.
God destroys the wicked by His breath.
God consumes them with the blast of His anger.
passages.original: מִנִּשְׁמַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ וּמֵר֖וּחַ אַפּ֣וֹ יִכְלֽוּ׃

passages.text: The lion may roar, and the fierce lion may growl, yet the teeth of the young lions are broken.
passages.sermon:
A lion roars.
A fierce lion growls.
The young lions have teeth.
But someone breaks the teeth of the young lions.
passages.original: שַׁאֲגַ֣ת אַ֭רְיֵה וְק֣וֹל שָׁ֑חַל וְשִׁנֵּ֖י כְפִירִ֣ים נִתָּֽעוּ׃

passages.text: The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
passages.sermon: The old lion dies when it has no prey.\r\nThe lioness’s cubs scatter.
passages.original: לַ֭יִשׁ אֹבֵ֣ד מִבְּלִי־ טָ֑רֶף וּבְנֵ֥י לָ֝בִ֗יא יִתְפָּרָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: Now a word came to me secretly; my ears caught a whisper of it.
passages.sermon: A word came to me in secret.\r\nMy ears heard a whisper of it.
passages.original: וְ֭אֵלַי דָּבָ֣ר יְגֻנָּ֑ב וַתִּקַּ֥ח אָ֝זְנִ֗י שֵׁ֣מֶץ מֶֽנְהֽוּ׃

passages.text: In disquieting visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on men, fear and trembling came over me and made all my bones shudder.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
He describes a personal experience.
He had troubling visions at night.
These visions came when people were in deep sleep.
Fear came over him.
Trembling seized him.
All his bones shook.
passages.original: בִּ֭שְׂעִפִּים מֵחֶזְיֹנ֣וֹת לָ֑יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֥ל תַּ֝רְדֵּמָ֗ה עַל־ אֲנָשִֽׁים׃ פַּ֣חַד קְ֭רָאַנִי וּרְעָדָ֑ה וְרֹ֖ב עַצְמוֹתַ֣י הִפְחִֽיד׃

passages.text: Then a spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body bristled.
passages.sermon: A spirit moved past my face.\r\nThe hair on my body stood up.
passages.original: וְ֭רוּחַ עַל־ פָּנַ֣י יַחֲלֹ֑ף תְּ֝סַמֵּ֗ר שַֽׂעֲרַ֥ת בְּשָׂרִֽי׃

passages.text: It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance; a form loomed before my eyes, and I heard a whispering voice: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than his Maker?
passages.sermon:
A spirit appeared before me at night.
It stood still in front of me.
I could not recognize its appearance.
A form was visible before my eyes.
I heard a quiet voice in the silence.
The voice asked a question.
It said, “Can a human be more righteous than God?”
It also said, “Can a man be more pure than his Maker?”
passages.original: יַעֲמֹ֤ד׀ וְֽלֹא־ אַכִּ֬יר מַרְאֵ֗הוּ תְּ֭מוּנָה לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י דְּמָמָ֖ה וָק֣וֹל אֶשְׁמָֽע׃ הַֽ֭אֱנוֹשׁ מֵאֱל֣וֹהַ יִצְדָּ֑ק אִ֥ם מֵ֝עֹשֵׂ֗הוּ יִטְהַר־ גָּֽבֶר׃

passages.text: If God puts no trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with error, how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who can be crushed like a moth!
passages.sermon:
God does not put His trust in His servants.
God finds fault even with His angels.
People live in bodies made of clay.
Their foundations are in the dust.
God can crush them easily, like a moth.
passages.original: הֵ֣ן בַּ֭עֲבָדָיו לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ין וּ֝בְמַלְאָכָ֗יו יָשִׂ֥ים תָּהֳלָֽה׃ אַ֤ף׀ שֹׁכְנֵ֬י בָֽתֵּי־ חֹ֗מֶר אֲשֶׁר־ בֶּעָפָ֥ר יְסוֹדָ֑ם יְ֝דַכְּא֗וּם לִפְנֵי־ עָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: They are smashed to pieces from dawn to dusk; unnoticed, they perish forever.
passages.sermon:
People live in houses made of clay.
Their bodies have foundations in the dust.
God can crush them easily.
From morning until evening, they are destroyed.
No one notices them.
They disappear forever.
passages.original: מִבֹּ֣קֶר לָעֶ֣רֶב יֻכַּ֑תּוּ מִבְּלִ֥י מֵ֝שִׂ֗ים לָנֶ֥צַח יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

passages.text: Are not their tent cords pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?’
passages.sermon:
People live in fragile bodies.
Their lives are like tents.
God removes their support.
Their lives end suddenly.
They die.
They do not gain wisdom.
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ נִסַּ֣ע יִתְרָ֣ם בָּ֑ם יָ֝מ֗וּתוּ וְלֹ֣א בְחָכְמָֽה׃
